limitations: All database/account/session/asset/provider fixtures are synthetic. No main merge, production deployment/migration, real account signup, live RPC/bank, signing key or actual transfer was performed.
Initial recovery covers exactly one explicitly activated pending or accepted initial marketplace cohort. The old mechanics fixture and an initialized-but-unactivated namespace remain unsupported.
Existing isolated-v3 and v2 correction formats remain distinct and reject this initial namespace. Original v1/v2/v3 commands, reducers, SQL invariants and frozen histories are unchanged.

Restore requires a fresh isolated target, preserves all original history, and appends exactly one pause. Source and targets remain paused; no authority re-entry, cross-instance leadership, provider reconciliation or resume is implemented.
Raw activation-basis timestamps must already use exact PostgreSQL UTC representation. Capture preserves native microseconds, large int8 strings and binary evidence; it refuses lossy JSON round trips.
Exact canonical and coordination table/column shapes are checked. This is not a general database dump or exhaustive inventory of arbitrary objects under alpha_wallet_simulation.

Canonical statement guards still reject row writes after early deferred checks; ordinary pending deferred completion rejects late mobile-authentication table creation. Hostile privileged DDL after deliberately draining all deferred events is outside the protocol.

Unknown-COMMIT evidence is a lost acknowledgement injected after an actual PostgreSQL COMMIT, not a physical network partition. Reconciliation reopens the same target and never overwrites a committed restore.
The native recovery race uses two actual database backends; exactly one fresh-target claim commits. PGlite cases alone do not establish that concurrency behavior.

Backups contain private retained financial payloads in plaintext. A checksum plus separately retained expected value establishes consistency, not authenticated provenance, freshness, encryption or restricted retention.
The implementation bounds and replays whole histories, repeating earlier replay/projection work during restore. It is not production throughput, availability, checkpointing, RPO or RTO evidence.
The Chromium gate is the retained standalone English/Arabic rehearsal, not integrated initial-cohort product screens or actual platform login. No native mobile or full production build was performed.
Root TypeScript excludes apps/mobile and the three existing excluded test paths in tsconfig.json. This development review is not an independent security audit.

Complete competing identity bindings, a new financial continuation for later lifecycle actions, real web/mobile product integration, custody/signing selection, fiat evidence policy and production operations remain open.
